But she quickly taking her cloake, couered her ſelfe. † And the ſeruant told Iſaac al things that he hed done. † Who brought her into the tent of Sara his mother, and tooke her to wife : and he loued her ſo much, that ir did moderate the ſorrowe, which was chanced, of his mothers death. Auguſtin teſtifieth ( li. de Gen. ad lit. c. & I. e. Neuertheles ſuch fignes are ſometimes lawfully obſerued, & deſired from God, as the ſame Doctor diſputeth (li. queſt. ſuper Gen q. 13) and S. Chriſo- ſtome teacheth more clerly (ho. in Gen) likewiſe S. Theodoret fa. in Gen) But whoſoeuer wil not erre in particular caſes, muſt folow either ex- preſſe Scripture, or the iudgement of the Church, whichis alwayes directed I by the ſpirite of truth. And touching this prayer of Abrahams ſeruant, and his deſire of this determinate ſigne, to know the maide, whom God had prouided to be Iſaachs wife, the fathers gencrally hold that it was religious, deuout, and diſcrere. For he being careful of his maſters buſines, and not truſting his. ovne iudgement, but relying vpon that Abraham had ſaid, Our Lord ihat Elierers pray- his Angrl heſore ther, commended ſo weightie a cauſe to God by prayer, the An- er, fora parti- gel ſuggeſting both to him to deſire, and to the maide to performe (as the e- uent ſhe woth ſuch qualities and vertues in her, as were moſt agreable to the great charitie and hoſpitalitie dayly practiſed in Abrahams houſe, moſt con- uenient and neceſſarie ( as he diſcretly conſidered) for that ſamilie, and good of manie. The like obſe ruations were approued in Gedeon, and Ionathas. And to vray for ſuch ſignes in ſome eaſe, or for manifeſt miracles is alſo approued by the Apoſtles example praying God To ſhevv by lote vvhich af the tvv he had choſen to the Apoſtleſhip, in place of indar. And that he would extend his hand to cures, & ſignes, & wonders, to be done by the name of his holie ſonne Iesvs. d.1. CHAP. XXV.
